# title: Aus Arthur Schopenhauers handschriftlichem Nachlaß. Abhandlungen, Anmerkungen, Aphorismen und Fragmente (1864)
# title_en: From Arthur Schopenhauer's manuscript remains: essays, annotations, aphorisms and fragments
# year: 1864
# edition: First printing: Aus Arthur Schopenhauers handschriftlichem Nachlaß. Abhandlungen, Anmerkungen, Aphorismen und Fragmente, hg. Julius Frauenstaedt, Leipzig: F. A. Brockhaus 1864; Internet Archive scan ausarthurschope00unkngoog, Google's text layer. The volume's own table of contents gives: I. Abhandlungen (1. Dialektik: Basis aller Dialektik, Kunstgriffe; Anhang: Ueber den Werth der Logik und ueber die Seltenheit der Urtheilskraft; 2. Ueber das Interessante; 3. Materialien zu einer Abhandlung ueber den argen Unfug mit der deutschen Sprache) - II. Anmerkungen (zu Kant: Prolegomena, Metaphysische Anfangsgruende der Tugendlehre, Dynamik, dritter mechanischer Grundsatz, Kritik der Urtheilskraft, Rechtslehre, Tugendlehre; zu Fichte; und weitere) - then Aphorismen und Fragmente.

# note: ADDED IN PASS 5, and it closes the worst hole in GAP-2: this volume contains the FIRST printing of the Eristische Dialektik ("Basis aller Dialektik" and "Kunstgriffe"), which until now was not in the collection in any language. It also prints Schopenhauer's annotations to Kant, which are primary and were never meant for the press. OCR warning: this scan is readable but it missets letters - b for d ("biefe" for "diese"), f for the long s ("fagen" for "sagen"), K for R ("Runftgriff" for "Kunstgriff") - and it garbles tables of contents; the long s has been normalised to s (12,047 of them). Printed pages could NOT be recovered, so cite by part and heading, not by page. Frauenstaedt's own note at "2. Kunstgriffe" explains the number of the stratagems; see the catalogue under P-08 and T3-07, because the popular "38 stratagems" is not what this first printing contains. PASS 17 PAGES: 275 printed pages recovered in pass 17 from running heads (a head counts only where its title repeats elsewhere in the file, and a page number only where it continues the sequence within twelve pages, since heads may be printed on recto only and the OCR drops some). Recovered, not invented: S. 4 to S. 475; where the OCR lost a head there is no marker, so a citation should be checked against the scan.

[Note of this collection, not part of the print: this is Google's OCR of the 1864 first printing, and its letter-level errors are NOT repaired - it prints b for d ("biefe" for "diese"), f for the long s ("fagen" for "sagen", "fein" for "sein"), and drops letters in headings and tables of contents. The long s itself has been normalised to s (12,047 of them) so that modern search works. Printed pages could NOT be recovered from this OCR - the folios came out as furniture - so a citation from this file gives the part and the heading, not a page number.]
